ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a large triangle JKL, J is at the lower left, L is at the lower right, and K is above; point A is located on side JK, and point B is located on side JL; segment AB is inside the triangle, and AB has the same arrow marking as the right side KL, indicating AB ∥ KL. Then reason: It is known that JL=27, BL=9, and B is on JL, so JB=JL−BL=27−9=18. Because AB ∥ KL, triangle JAB and triangle JKL are similar. Corresponding sides are proportional: JA/JK = JB/JL. Substituting JK=18, JB=18, JL=27, get JA/18 = 18/27 = 2/3. Therefore JA = 18 × 2/3 = 12.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a large triangle JKL with A on side JK and B on side JL, and with segment AB marked parallel to side KL. From the text use JL=27, BL=9, and JK=18. method.method_draft: Read from the diagram that AB is drawn inside triangle JKL with AB parallel to KL, cutting sides JK and JL at A and B. From the text, JL=27 and BL=9, so JB=18. Apply the side-splitter theorem: the parallel segment divides the two sides proportionally, so JA/AK = JB/BL = 18/9 = 2. Thus JA:AK = 2:1. Since the whole side JK=18, JA is two of the three equal ratio parts, so JA = (2/3)·18 = 12.
